state.objective: A concise source language must carry an authored message language to server display and show explicit formatter results without changing their selected language, while preserving legacy calls and refusing incompatible consumers.
verified_current_facts: The checked compiler message owner has a source-language tag. Its public UI message descriptor currently contains source text, locale variants and optional bound typed parameters; the public constructor has three arguments and omits that language.

The presentation resolver has an optional separate source-locale option with legacy English default. Plural grammar uses its selected variant locale. Imported message assets retain their checked declaring owner.

The public message formatter already returns a frozen exact object with text and selected locale. A generated helper supplies selected-app default, checked source language and admitted team timezone. Existing pure expression consumers use that complete object.

Public display values admit strings, exact scalar carriers and message descriptors, but do not admit that formatter object. Compiler provenance currently refuses all formatted results at UI and business sinks; exact plain-text values is the selected next UI slot.

A message descriptor is an unresolved pattern plus parameters. A formatter result is literal text plus effective language. Already-formatted text must never be parsed as a pattern, re-resolved for the viewer, implicitly coerced to a string, or admitted to business effects by this change.

The existing public locale-resolution result has the same text/locale structural pair. Resolution alone may return a pattern; generated producer provenance must remain explicit even if the display carrier shares this structure.

The module assembler checks that the installed UI file exists and binds generated imports. It does not enforce the public presentation version constant. Known artifact capability requirements are checked by another host path; an unknown new requirement is refused.

JavaScript old three-argument constructors silently ignore a fourth argument. A source-language extension therefore needs an actual consumer support check. Older display renderers already refuse the formatter object through scalar validation.

Old three-argument messages must retain English source default. These transient display values do not change stored business rows, session identities, action data, or durable receipts. No deployment or general migration is authorized.

The concrete consumer can use an imported French source message at zero, where French and English plural selection differ, plus an explicit formatter result shown under another viewer locale. Output must preserve effective language, HTML escaping and bidirectional isolation. Other UI props, business calls and outbound human sinks remain unclassified/refused.
